findings.title: Should the quillsort tool accept its arguments in either order?
findings.situation: In the week the tool was called 40 times and failed 10 times, a quarter of its calls: 6 failures in the first group [E-001.errors=6] and 4 in the second [E-002.errors=4], so 6 + 4 = 10 failures, matching the query total [Q-001#0.errors=10]. The week before, the baseline was 1 failure in 20 calls.
findings.history: First seen on 2026-01-29. No earlier ruling exists; this is the first time seen.
findings.problem: Calls fail when the sort key comes before the file name, and each failure is retried by hand.
findings.why_problem: The tool parses its arguments by position and rejects a swapped pair with a vague message, so the caller cannot tell what to fix and tries the same call again.
findings.impact: 10 failed calls, each followed by one retry of about 2 minutes, so about 20 minutes (10 retries x 2 minutes) of lost work in the week; the 2 minute figure is an estimate from the sample sessions.

options.name: Do nothing
options.cons: About 20 minutes a week keep being lost.
options.if_ruled: Nothing changes and no work bead is filed.

options.name: Accept the arguments in either order
options.pros: Removes the whole class of failure.
options.cons: A small change to the tool settings is needed.
options.if_ruled: If you adopt this, one work bead is filed in the workspace tracker for the settings repo.

recommendation.option: Accept the arguments in either order
recommendation.why: It removes the cause for a small, one-time edit.

glossary.meaning: The same measure over the week before the window, used for comparison.
